subsystems.name: Design space
subsystems.role: the parametric geometry the agent is allowed to search — parts, features, materials and joining methods.

subsystems.name: Performance simulators
subsystems.role: predict whether a candidate design actually works before anything is made.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing simulator
subsystems.role: works out how the part would be made and how long it would take.

subsystems.name: Robot co-design module
subsystems.role: given the product, searches for an arm, gantry or cell layout that can build it.

subsystems.name: Search controller
subsystems.role: the agent that proposes, scores, prunes and re-proposes across both loops.

subsystems.name: Physical validation rig
subsystems.role: closes the loop against reality rather than a model.
parts: test cell with a robot and sensors
calibration data feed back to simulators

buildSteps.title: Write the requirement envelope
buildSteps.detail: Fix the loads the product must carry, allowable mass, materials, tolerances, the factory floor space and the budget. Everything the agent is allowed to change is declared here, and nothing else.

buildSteps.title: Build the design space
buildSteps.detail: Encode the product as parameters in a CAD kernel, with a library of features that are known to be manufacturable, so the search cannot wander into shapes no machine could make.

buildSteps.title: Wire up the simulators
buildSteps.detail: Attach structural, thermal and cost models to the geometry, using fast surrogate models trained on slower high-fidelity runs so thousands of candidates can be scored per hour.

buildSteps.title: Close the inner loop
buildSteps.detail: The agent iterates on the product alone — topology optimisation to strip mass, then sizing — keeping the best candidates in a population rather than a single answer.

buildSteps.title: Close the outer loop
buildSteps.detail: For a shortlisted product, the agent searches cell configurations: robot type, number of axes, reach, payload, tooling and fixture layout, and re-times the assembly.

buildSteps.title: Feed manufacturability back
buildSteps.detail: The outer loop changes what the inner loop may propose — a part that needs five setups is penalised if the co-designed cell can only do three. Iterate the two loops jointly, since neither is optimal alone.

buildSteps.title: Resolve the trade-off
buildSteps.detail: Run a bilevel search in which the outer loop optimises the cell and the inner loop re-optimises the product for that cell, repeating until the pair stops improving.

buildSteps.title: Validate physically
buildSteps.detail: Machine or print one instance, build the cell in simulation against a digital twin of the real installation, then build it for real and measure.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and freeze
buildSteps.detail: Compare measured cycle times, deflections and defects with predictions, correct the simulators, and iterate once or twice before the design and cell are certified and released.

prerequisites.why: decades old and now commercial; it produces single parts, not whole products plus their factory.

prerequisites.tech: Fast differentiable or surrogate physics simulation
prerequisites.why: the search needs answers in seconds, not hours, and no general-purpose solver does that reliably yet.
optimising a robot's body and its controller together is demonstrated in research, rarely beyond it.
deciding the sequence of operations and fixtures is still largely done by human manufacturing engineers.

prerequisites.tech: Agent planners that drive engineering tools
prerequisites.why: language-model agents can call CAD and solver APIs, but cannot yet be trusted to run a search unattended.

prerequisites.tech: Verification and certification of machine-generated designs
prerequisites.why: regulators and customers need to know why a design is safe when no engineer chose it.

pathway.milestone: generative design used for individual brackets and housings, with humans choosing and validating
pathway.unlocks: proof that optimisation can beat hand design on mass and stiffness.

pathway.milestone: agents that propose a part and its tooling and fixture together, checked by an engineer
pathway.unlocks: shorter design-to-manufacture cycles for low-volume and bespoke parts.

pathway.milestone: co-designed robot cells: the arm and the product optimised as one system, validated in a real cell
pathway.unlocks: cells built around one product family, cheaply reconfigurable when the product changes.

pathway.milestone: closed loop where a validated search output goes straight to production with sampled human audit
pathway.unlocks: design cycles measured in days for parts nobody has made before — the real prize.

pathway.milestone: agents that design their own successors' hardware
pathway.unlocks: faster iteration, but also the hardest questions about verification and control.
